text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Philippine President Fidel Ramos held wide-ranging talks with Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, after which the two countries signed an agreement on use of nuclear energy.
- Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said the agencies that he was relying on to carry out accountability themselves need reform.
- The committees set up to give proposals for revival of industrial activity and economic growth will submit their recommendations within a week.
- Senate chairman Waseem Sajjad is tipped to retain his post after elections to the upper house later this month. It would be his third term in the office.
- A four-member delegation led by Mushahid Hussain, information adviser to the prime minister, will visit the United States to raise funds for the debt retirement scheme.
- Punjab Chief Minister Shahbaz Sharif said anti-state elements were trying to harm Pakistan and Iran relations.
- Indian border security forces and Pakistani rangers traded fire twice across the borderline near the town of Sialkot, military sources said.
- Indian Foreign Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said talks with Pakistan this month would address all issues of mutual concern.
- Banks failing to transfer funds raised under the National Debt Retirement Programme to the State (central) Bank of Pakistan within 48 hours will be charged 22 percent a year.
- Pakistan and Philippines signed two agreements on mutual cooperation and also decided to set up a business council for promotion of trade between the two countries.
- The ministry of petroleum and natural resources has formed a high level committee to monitor the quality of petroleum products being supplied in Pakistan.
- The commissioning of three new polyester staple fibre plants in the first quarter of 1997 is expected to boost polyester yarn and fabric exports by 30 percent.
- Water levels in the main power generating dams of Terbela and Mangla are low due to the continued dry spell. The country will face an acute shortage of electricity and water for irrigation.
